Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No specific evidence found of agriculture system (farmer registries, subsidies) integration with Tanzania's data exchange platform. Agricultural data systems exist independently.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original citation (GovESB homepage only) did not evidence agriculture integration. Ministry of Agriculture's FY2026/27 budget speech (Hotuba ya Bajeti, tabled 25 April 2026), as reported by Kilimo Kwanza, confirms the e-Kilimo (Integrated Kilimo System) platform is integrated with NIDA, TRA, TANCIS, BRELA, GePG, NHIF, TFRA, the Cooperative Development Commission (via MUVU) and TMA, underpinning farmer registration and a digital input-voucher/subsidy programme covering roughly 5.4 million beneficiaries. Land registration and extension-service (BBT-Ugani) integration are described as still being built rather than complete, so full integration is not yet evidenced. Score raised from 0 (Unknown) to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: Tanzania's e-Kilimo (Integrated Kilimo System) platform, run by the Ministry of Agriculture, is integrated with several national government systems, including the National Identification Authority (NIDA) for identity verification, the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) and Tanzania Customs Integrated System (TANCIS) for tax records, the Business Registrations and Licensing Agency (BRELA), the Government electronic Payment Gateway (GePG) for digital disbursement, the National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF), the Tanzania Fertilizer Regulatory Authority (TFRA), the Cooperative Development Commission via the MUVU system, and the Tanzania Meteorological Authority (TMA). This underpins farmer registration and a digital input-voucher/subsidy programme covering an estimated 5.4 million beneficiaries, as set out in the Ministry's FY2026/27 budget speech. Land administration and agricultural-extension data integration are still being developed, so integration with the wider data exchange remains partial rather than complete.

Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No specific evidence found of electoral register integration with GovESB or Jamii X-Change. NEC (National Electoral Commission) systems appear siloed. Planned under broader digital government integration.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: GovESB homepage citation does not itself confirm or deny electoral integration. e-GA's official list of institutions connected to GovESB (22 Dec 2022) names NIDA, BRELA, the Judiciary, insurance authorities, the Tanzania Commission for Universities and the Attorney-General's Office, but not the National Electoral Commission (NEC). e-GA's 2017 Integration Architecture standard uses NEC voter registration as an illustrative worked example of how the ESB could operate, but this is a design illustration, not evidence of live operational integration. No authoritative source confirms electoral-register integration with the data exchange platform, so the score of 0 (Unknown) is confirmed.
revised_comments: No authoritative evidence confirms that Tanzania's National Electoral Commission voter-registration systems (the Permanent National Voters' Register and related Integrated Election Management Systems) are integrated with the Government Enterprise Service Bus or Jamii X-Change data exchange platforms. The Commission's own systems are integrated internally with one another but appear to operate independently of the national data exchange infrastructure.

Definition: Integration of job seeker registries, unemployment insurance, public employment programs, labor market information
Comments: No specific evidence of employment/labor market data integration with Tanzania data exchange platform. Ministry of Labour systems appear separate.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: GovESB homepage citation does not itself confirm status. TaESA's standalone jobseeker/employer portal, run by the Prime Minister's Office (Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disability), provides job matching and labour-market information but no evidence links it to GovESB or Jamii X-Change. e-GA's published list of institutions connected to GovESB does not include TaESA or other Ministry of Labour systems. Score of 0 (Unknown) confirmed.
revised_comments: Tanzania's employment services, delivered through the TaESA online jobseeker/employer portal under the Prime Minister's Office (Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disability), operate as a standalone system. No evidence indicates this platform, or wider labour-market and unemployment-insurance data, is integrated with the Government Enterprise Service Bus (GovESB) or the Jamii X-Change data exchange platform.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: No evidence found of justice/court system integration with GovESB or Jamii X-Change. Judiciary systems appear separate.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 cited only the GovESB homepage, which does not itself confirm or deny justice-sector integration. An official e-GA announcement (22 Dec 2022) explicitly lists the Judiciary (Mahakama) among institutions connected to GovESB, alongside NIDA, BRELA, insurance authorities, the Tanzania Commission for Universities and the Attorney-General's Office. The current GovESB dashboard also lists Legal/Constitutional and Legal Affairs among active data-exchange sectors. The scope and depth of data actually exchanged with the Judiciary is not publicly detailed, so the score is raised to 4 (Partially integrated) rather than 5 (Fully integrated).
revised_comments: Tanzania's Judiciary (Mahakama) is one of the public institutions connected to the Government Enterprise Service Bus (GovESB), alongside the National Identification Authority (NIDA), the Business Registration and Licensing Agency (BRELA), insurance regulators, the Tanzania Commission for Universities and the Attorney-General's Office, according to the e-Government Authority. The Judiciary separately operates its own Electronic Case Management System (JoT-eCMS) for case filing and tracking. The precise scope of data exchanged between the Judiciary and other government systems via GovESB is not publicly documented, indicating partial rather than comprehensive integration.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No evidence of AI/analytics integrated into Tanzania's data exchange platform (GovESB or Jamii X-Change). Novissi-style AI not present here.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original sources (GovESB homepage and DPI Africa case study) do not address AI/analytics specifically. The Citizen (7 Feb 2024) reports the e-Government Authority's director-general confirming Tanzania is considering AI adoption within GovESB and wider e-government platforms to upgrade the national digital data pool. e-GA's 2024 Technology Roadmap lists Artificial Intelligence, IoT and Big Data/data-mining as forthcoming technology-roadmap items rather than functioning capabilities. Score raised from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (Planned), as no evidence shows AI piloted or functional within the exchange itself.
revised_comments: Artificial intelligence is not yet functional within Tanzania's data exchange system. The e-Government Authority has stated it is considering AI adoption across the Government Enterprise Service Bus (GovESB) and wider e-government platforms to strengthen the national digital data pool, and its 2024 Technology Roadmap lists Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things and Big Data/data-mining capabilities as forthcoming rather than deployed technologies.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: eGA publishes annual reports and documentation on GovESB. Jamii X-Change case study publicly available. e-Government Strategy documents published. Moderate transparency through eGA website and ICTC publications. No real-time public dashboard.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Original score of 3 (Moderate — Annual Reports) was based on the eGA website and Jamii X-Change case study, and stated there was 'no real-time public dashboard'. A live public GovESB Dashboard Portal (dashboard.govesb.gov.go.tz) was found and fetched directly: it reports real-time statistics — connected systems (282), systems exchanging data (514), connected institutions (204), new endpoints (868), systems without connection (39) — plus top producer/consumer institutions and a live interoperability connection map, filterable by sector. This meets the scale's top tier (Public Dashboard & Reports) rather than Moderate, so the score is raised from 3 to 4.
revised_comments: Tanzania's data exchange governance is transparent to a high standard. The e-Government Authority operates a live, publicly accessible GovESB Dashboard Portal reporting real-time statistics on connected systems, systems exchanging data, connected institutions, new endpoints and an interoperability connection map, filterable by date and sector, alongside published annual reports, technology roadmaps and the Jamii X-Change case study documentation. This combination of a public real-time dashboard and published reporting represents a high level of transparency.
